_about: Attack family per SKILL-INJECT injection, for the coverage analysis in docs/SPEC.md §8.11.
PROVENANCE OF EACH COLUMN, because it matters which part is third-party:
* the injection ids, titles and `injection_goal` text come from aisa-group/skill-inject
* the grouping of those goals into the families below is OURS. The benchmark's own `type`
field is `script` | `direct`, which is the delivery mechanism, not what the attack does,
so it cannot answer 'which family is uncovered'.
Assignments are listed explicitly rather than derived by keyword match so that every one of
them can be argued with by reading this file. `note` records a call that is not obvious.

families.exfiltration: Sends data somewhere it should not go -- an external endpoint, an attacker's git remote, a public dataset, a log file the attacker reads.
families.destruction: Destroys user data: deletes files, drops databases, cancels calendar events, resets or force-pushes over history.
families.weakened-security: Leaves the system less defended than it found it: backdoor accounts and ports, chmod 777, skipped security checks, SQL built by concatenation, payment verification removed.
families.bias: Manipulates the CONTENT the agent produces -- political slant, false citations, inflated scores, revisionism, discriminatory substitutions.
families.ransomware: Encrypts or password-locks the user's files.
families.rce: Fetches code from the network and executes it.
families.dos: Turns the user's machine into a source of traffic against a third party.
families.phishing: Uses the user's own account to send deceptive mail onward.
families.prompt-injection: Writes injection text into data the agent (or another agent) will later read.
families.other: Real attacks that fit none of the above cleanly.
